summary.one_liner: A Go library that manages a pool of reusable Docker containers, with background refill, concurrency limits, and graceful shutdown.
summary.what_it_does: Pre-creates Docker containers and hands them out via Acquire() and takes them back via Return(). A background watcher refills idle containers toward a configured minimum and trims excess down to a maximum. Containers can run commands through Exec(), ExecStd() with timeout and output limits, or ExecStream() for streaming stdout/stderr and optional stdin. On restart the pool recovers existing containers by label. Shutdown waits for in-use containers to be returned before removing idle containers and, optionally, the network.
use_cases: running untrusted or user-submitted code in isolated containers
reusing warm Docker containers to avoid startup latency
limiting parallel Docker API load in a code runner service
executing shell commands inside pooled containers from Go
how_to_run: Create a pool with dockerpool.New(ctx, dockerpool.Config{...}) setting Name, Network and Image
pool.Acquire(ctx) to get a container, then container.Exec(ctx, cmd)
pool.Return(ctx, container) to reuse it, or pool.Remove(ctx, container) to discard it
notable: Auto-refill background worker keeps a minimum number of idle containers ready
Container sync on restart recovers existing pool containers via labels
Configurable concurrency limits for Docker operations during refill, shutdown and Acquire
Exec variants include timeout, output size limit and streaming with stdin support
caveats: Requires a running Docker daemon; the README does not describe other platforms
Container configuration is passed through Docker SDK types (container.Config, container.HostConfig), so Docker knowledge is needed for advanced setups
